Amid that poisoned atmosphere, Spain will play the hosts with the World Cup winners living the very opposite to that of the Balkan side. These are days of wine and roses, a “honeymoon,” as Santi Denia said last Friday before the match against the Czech Republic. More than 40 matches unbeaten, world champions, winners of their first three games in the Nations League 2026-27, Luis de la Fuente has navigated the many absences from the long international break (Porro, Eric, Ferran, Grimaldo, Nico, Fabián) and has moved his pieces with mastery. Only Lamine has started the previous three matches. Because, although De la Fuente says he is just one more, Lamine is Lamine. And a global star of his stature already has special treatment. The same happens at Barça with Flick, and it is inevitable. And Lamine likes to play and with that in mind, the coach managed his minutes wisely at the Carlos Tartiere. Starter or substitute, he will play. In three games he has scored four superb goals and provided an assist. It is hard not to see him in the starting XI.
